head: PolicyNest POSP Onboarding Rulebook v3.2
text:
> **Operating Standard** — PolicyNest Insurance Brokers (Fictional)  
> **Effective Date:** 1 April 2026  
> **Source:** Masters' Union Applied AI Challenge (PS-01 AI-First Onboarding)

---

head: Notice
text:
**SYNTHETIC DATASET NOTICE:** This document is the exact operating standard developed for the Masters' Union Applied AI Challenge. Names, identifiers, numbers, and events described are synthetic. Eligibility rules follow the published IRDAI framework for Point of Sales Persons (POSP). Where PolicyNest applies a stricter internal rule, it is marked **Internal**.

---

PS-01 · DATA PACK

PolicyNest Insurance Brokers (fictional) · Onboarding Ops standard v3.2 · effective 1 April 2026

head: 1. Purpose and scope
text:
This rulebook is the operating standard PolicyNest's Onboarding Ops team uses to decide whether a person can be certified as a Point of Sales Person (POSP) for general and life insurance. It covers eligibility, the documents we collect, how each document is checked, how mismatches between documents are resolved, when to ask the applicant for more information and when to reject. It is written for human reviewers today. Your product should apply the same rules, explain each decision in these terms, and leave the decisions marked Human only to a person.

Eligibility rules in section 2 follow the published IRDAI framework for POSPs. Where PolicyNest applies a stricter internal rule, it is marked Internal. Students should check the current IRDAI text themselves before treating any rule as regulatory.

head: 2. Eligibility
text:
| Rule | Requirement | Evidence | If not met |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Age | 18 years or older on the date the application is started | DOB on PAN; cross-checked with Aadhaar and Class 10 marksheet | REJECT — UNDERAGE |
| Education | Passed Class 10 (secondary) from a recognised board, including NIOS | Class 10 marksheet or certificate showing PASS | REJECT — EDU_NOT_ELIGIBLE |
| Identity | Valid individual PAN (4th character P) | PAN card | REJECT — PAN_FORMAT_INVALID or PAN_NOT_INDIVIDUAL |
| Exclusivity | Not already registered as a POSP with another insurer or intermediary | IRDAI POSP registry lookup on PAN | REJECT — ALREADY_REGISTERED (applicant may reapply after a no-objection certificate) |
| Training | Complete 15 hours of POSP training | Training platform log | Cannot sit exam |
| Examination | Pass the POSP examination | Exam result | Re-attempt allowed after 24 hours |
| Bank account | Savings or current account in the applicant's own name, for commission | Cancelled cheque or bank statement + penny-drop | NEEDS_INFO — BANK_NAME_MISMATCH |

head: 3. Documents we collect
text:
PAN card — the anchor document. Name and date of birth on the PAN are treated as the reference values for every other check.

Aadhaar, front and back — identity and address. Only the last four digits of the Aadhaar number are ever stored; any image showing all twelve digits must be masked before storage.

Class 10 marksheet or certificate — education eligibility and a second source for name and DOB.

Cancelled cheque or the first page of a bank statement — account holder name, IFSC and account number for commission payouts.

Selfie — a live photo compared with the PAN photo by the face-match service. Scores are from 0 to 1.

Optional: GST certificate (for agents above the GST threshold), address proof if the current address differs from Aadhaar.

head: 4.1 Image quality (all documents)
text:
All four corners visible. If a corner or edge field is missing: REUPLOAD — IMAGE_CROPPED.

Every field legible at normal zoom. If any required field cannot be read with confidence: REUPLOAD — IMAGE_BLURRY.

No reflection covering a field. If a reflection hides a field: REUPLOAD — IMAGE_GLARE.

A photocopy or a photo of a screen is accepted only for the bank document; for identity documents ask for a photo of the original (Internal).

OCR confidence below 0.75 should be treated as a likely quality problem and checked, not trusted.

head: 4.2 PAN
text:
Format: five letters, four digits, one letter (AAAAA9999A). Anything else: REJECT — PAN_FORMAT_INVALID.

The 4th character shows the holder type. Only P (individual) is eligible. C (company), F (firm), H (HUF), T (trust) and others: REJECT — PAN_NOT_INDIVIDUAL.

The 5th character is normally the first letter of the holder's surname. A mismatch is not by itself a reason to reject, but should raise attention when combined with other inconsistencies.

The PAN typed by the applicant must equal the PAN on the card. A single-character difference is usually a typing error: correct it from the card and log the correction.

head: 4.3 Aadhaar
text:
Store only the last four digits. Never write the full number to any system, log or prompt.

Name must match the PAN under the name-matching rules in section 5.

DOB must equal the PAN DOB. Some older Aadhaar cards show only the year of birth; a year-only value that matches the PAN year is acceptable.

The address state may differ from the declared state — agents often work away from home. This is informational and never a reason to reject.

head: 4.4 Class 10 marksheet
text:
Result must read PASS (or show passing marks in every compulsory subject where no result line exists).

Accept any state board, CBSE, CISCE or NIOS. Marksheets from boards not on the recognised list are Human only.

Name must match the PAN under section 5. A spelling difference here is common because marksheets are older than PAN cards.

DOB on the marksheet should match the PAN. If they differ, the PAN is treated as correct only if the Aadhaar agrees with the PAN; otherwise NEEDS_INFO — DOB_MISMATCH.

head: 4.5 Bank document
text:
The account must be in the applicant's own name. Joint accounts are accepted if the applicant is the first holder.

IFSC format: four letters, a zero, six alphanumeric characters.

The penny-drop check returns the account holder name from the bank. It must match the PAN name under section 5. If it does not: NEEDS_INFO — BANK_NAME_MISMATCH.

A spouse's or parent's account is never accepted, whatever the explanation.

head: 4.6 Selfie
text:
Face-match score ≥ 0.75: accept.

0.60–0.75: Human only — a reviewer compares the photos.

Below 0.60: NEEDS_INFO — FACE_MATCH_LOW. Ask for a fresh selfie in good light.

head: 5. Name matching — the rules that cause most rework
text:
Indian names appear in many legitimate forms across documents issued years apart. Reviewers spend more time on names than on anything else, and they disagree with each other more often on names than on anything else. The rules below are how a decision should be made.

| Pattern | Example (PAN → other document) | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exact (ignoring case and spacing) | RAHUL KUMAR SHARMA → Rahul Kumar Sharma | Match |
| Initials for given or middle names | RAHUL KUMAR SHARMA → R K SHARMA | Match |
| Order swapped | RAHUL KUMAR SHARMA → SHARMA RAHUL KUMAR | Match |
| Middle name missing | RAHUL KUMAR SHARMA → RAHUL SHARMA | Match |
| Middle name added | PRIYA SHARMA → PRIYA KUMARI SHARMA | Match |
| Spelling variant of the same name | MOHAMMAD ASIF → MOHAMMED ASIF; LAKSHMI → LAXMI | NEEDS_INFO — NAME_SPELLING_VARIANT |
| Surname changed after marriage | PRIYA SHARMA → PRIYA VERMA | NEEDS_INFO — ask for marriage certificate or gazette notification (Human only) |

When in doubt between a spelling variant and a different person, prefer NEEDS_INFO and route to a human. A wrongful rejection costs us a good agent; a wrongful approval of a different person is a compliance breach.

head: 6. Making the application-level decision
text:
Collect every document-level finding.

If any finding is a REJECT reason, the application is REJECT. Give every reason, not only the first.

Otherwise, if any finding is a NEEDS_INFO or REUPLOAD reason, the application is NEEDS_MORE_INFO. Ask for everything that is needed in a single message — today's process asks one thing at a time, and each round trip adds about two days.

Otherwise the application is APPROVE and moves to training.

Informational findings (address state differs, PAN 5th character unusual) are recorded but never change the decision on their own.

head: 7. Service levels and escalation
text:
| Step | Target | Escalate to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First review after documents submitted | 4 working hours | Team lead after 8 hours |
| Review after re-upload | 2 working hours | Team lead after 4 hours |
| Applicant query by phone or WhatsApp | 1 working hour | Team lead |

head: 8. Messages to applicants
text:
Messages go out by WhatsApp and SMS in English or Hindi. They must say exactly what is wrong, what to send, and how.

Re-upload: "Your Class 10 marksheet photo is blurry, so we could not read your date of birth. Please take a new photo in daylight with all four corners visible and upload it here: <link>."

Bank name mismatch: "The bank account you shared is not in your name. Commission can only be paid into your own account. Please upload a cancelled cheque or statement for an account in your name."

Spelling variant: "Your name is spelt differently on your PAN (MOHAMMAD) and marksheet (MOHAMMED). Please upload either a corrected document or a signed declaration in the attached format."

Rejection (underage): "You must be 18 or older to register. You can apply again from <date>."

head: 9. Decisions that stay with a human
text:
Any REJECT for NAME_MISMATCH (a different person) — the system may recommend, a person confirms.

Face-match scores between 0.60 and 0.75.

Marksheets from boards not on the recognised list.

Surname changes after marriage.

Any case the applicant disputes.

head: 10. What good looks like
text: A reviewer who follows this rulebook well decides a clean application in under five minutes and asks for everything missing in one message. The best reviewers on the team certify agents in under three days end to end. The team average is far slower, mainly because of one-at-a-time document requests and queue waiting, not because any single check is hard.

head: IRDAI Regulatory Framework Reference for POSP Onboarding
text:
> **Statutory Compendium of Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India Mandates**  
> **Key Regulations:** IRDAI/INT/GDL/ECM/044/03/2017 & Insurance Brokers Regulations 2018  
> **Compliance Context:** Point of Sales Person (POSP) Certification & Life/General Insurance Distribution

---

head: 1. Statutory Definition & Scope of POSP
text:
Under IRDAI Guidelines (Circular IRDAI/INT/GDL/ECM/044/03/2017), a **Point of Sales Person (POSP)** is defined as:
> *"An individual who solicits and markets pre-underwritten, simplified insurance products approved by the Authority, acting on behalf of an insurer or an insurance intermediary."*

head: 1.1 Permitted Insurance Products
text:
POSPs are strictly authorized to distribute pre-underwritten products where coverage, premium tables, and underwriting rules are fully automated and do not require individual underwriter discretion:
- **Motor Insurance:** Mandatory Third-Party (TP) liability and comprehensive packages for private cars, two-wheelers, and commercial vehicles.
- **Health Insurance:** Fixed-benefit health policies, critical illness plans, and individual/family indemnity covers up to regulatory sub-limits (typically sum insured up to ₹5 Lakhs).
- **Personal Accident Insurance:** Standard personal accident and accidental death/disability policies.
- **Travel Insurance:** Domestic and overseas travel insurance covers.
- **Life Insurance:** Pure term insurance policies without medical examination requirement, immediate annuities, and simplified non-linked endowment products.

---

head: 2.1 Minimum Age (§4.a)
text:
- The candidate must have completed **eighteen (18) years of age** on the date of application.
- *Statutory Evidence:* Date of birth recorded on Permanent Account Number (PAN) card, Aadhaar card, or Birth Certificate.

head: 2.2 Minimum Educational Qualification (§4.b)
text:
- The candidate must have passed at least the **10th standard (Secondary School Examination)** or equivalent examination from a recognized State Board, Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE), Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations (CISCE), or National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS).
- *Statutory Evidence:* Class 10 marksheet or pass certificate displaying candidate name, father's name, date of birth, and `PASS` outcome.

head: 2.3 Identity & Tax Integrity
text:
- Valid individual PAN card issued by the Income Tax Department (4th character `'P'`).
- Linking with Aadhaar under PMLA guidelines.

---

head: 3.1 15-Hour Mandatory Training Curriculum (§5)
text:
- Every aspiring POSP must undergo a mandatory **15 hours of structured training** conducted by the sponsoring insurer or insurance broker.
- The curriculum must comprehensively cover:
  1. Fundamentals of Insurance & Principles of Utmost Good Faith (*Uberrimae Fidei*).
  2. Structure and Types of General and Life Insurance Contracts.
  3. Pre-underwritten POSP product features, exclusions, and limits.
  4. Proposal form filling, premium calculation, and digital issuance.
  5. Claims reporting and grievance redressal mechanisms.
  6.
- *Compliance Requirement:* The platform LMS must maintain auditable time logs verifying that the applicant spent at least 15.0 active hours completing the curriculum before being admitted to the certification exam.

head: 3.2 Examination & Certification (§6)
text:
- The candidate must appear for and pass a proctored examination administered by the sponsor in accordance with IRDAI guidelines.
- Successful candidates are awarded a digital **POSP Certificate of Registration** bearing a unique registration number, sponsor broker details, and validity terms.
- A 24-hour mandatory waiting period is required before any re-examination attempt in the event of an initial examination failure.

---

head: 4. The Exclusivity Register & Central De-Registration Rules
text:
Under Section 7 of the POSP Guidelines:
1. **Single-Sponsor Exclusivity:** A POSP can be sponsored by and registered with only **one** general insurer/broker and **one** life insurer/broker at any given point in time.
2. **Central Registry Verification:** Prior to onboarding, the sponsoring intermediary must query the central POSP registry maintained by the Insurance Information Bureau of India (IIB) using the candidate's PAN number.
3. **De-Registration Protocol:** If a candidate is already registered with another entity:
   - The application must be rejected under code `ALREADY_REGISTERED`.
   - The candidate must obtain a formal **No Objection Certificate (NOC)** or surrender certificate from the existing sponsor.
   - The previous sponsor must remove the POSP from the central IIB register before PolicyNest can legally complete certification.

---

head: 5. Intermediary Liabilities & Compliance Audits
text:
Under the IRDAI (Insurance Brokers) Regulations, 2018:
1. **Principal-Agent Liability:** PolicyNest Insurance Brokers is vicariously liable for all acts of solicitation, misrepresentation, or misconduct committed by its certified POSPs.
2. **Record Retention:** All KYC records, proof of education, bank details, training logs, exam scores, and issuance timestamps must be maintained in an immutable, auditable archive for a minimum of **five (5) years** from the date of certification or termination.
3. **Statutory Penalties:** Sponsoring ineligible candidates (e.g., underage or failing Class 10 education), failing to maintain training records, or distributing non-POS products through POSP channels attracts statutory sanctions, fines, and potential cancellation of the broker license under IRDAI inspection.

head: IRDAI Regulatory Requirements Matrix & PolicyNest Operating Rules
text:
This document provides the authoritative regulatory and compliance mapping for the PolicyNest AI-First POSP Onboarding Platform. It synthesises statutory mandates issued by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI), the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), the Income Tax Department (CBDT), and the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act 2023 with PolicyNest's internal operational rules (Rulebook v3.2).

---

head: 1. Statutory & Regulatory Foundation
text:
The Point of Sales Person (POSP) distribution model in India is governed by the following core regulatory instruments:
1. **IRDAI Guidelines on Point of Sales Person - Life and General Insurance:**
   - Circular Ref: IRDAI/INT/GDL/ECM/044/03/2017 (and subsequent updates).
   - Allows insurance intermediaries (brokers, corporate agents) and insurers to sponsor POSPs to solicit and market pre-underwritten, simplified insurance products.
2. **IRDAI (Insurance Brokers) Regulations, 2018:**
   - Establishes broker responsibility for training, examination, KYC verification, code of conduct, and maintaining the central register of POSPs.
3. **IRDAI Central POSP Registry (IIB / Insurance Information Bureau):**
   - Mandates exclusivity: a POSP can be sponsored by and registered with only **one** life insurer/broker and **one** general insurer/broker at any given time.
4. **UIDAI Aadhaar Regulations & Section 8A of Aadhaar Act 2016:**
   - Prohibits storage of full 12-digit Aadhaar numbers in plaintext. Strict masking (storing only last 4 digits `XXXX-XXXX-1234`) is mandatory for non-banking private entities unless authorised via Aadhaar e-KYC.
5. **Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023:**
   - Mandates lawful processing based on explicit consent, purpose limitation, storage limitation, data minimization, and audit trail of data processing.

---

head: 3. Human vs Autonomous AI Decision Boundaries
text: Under IRDAI governance guidelines and PolicyNest Risk Controls, autonomous AI straight-through processing (STP) is strictly constrained:

head: 3.1 Decisions Permitted for Autonomous AI (STP)
text:
- **STP Approval:** Granted **ONLY** when:
  1. All 5 required documents present.
  2. Image quality is OK on all documents (OCR confidence >= 0.75, no blur, no glare, no crop).
  3. Age >= 18 verified across PAN, Aadhaar, 10th.
  4. Class 10 education passed from recognized board.
  5. Individual PAN format validated (`P` as 4th char).
  6. IRDAI POSP registry check returns clean (no hit).
  7. Name matching conforms strictly to Tier 1 (Exact), Tier 2 (Initials), Tier 3 (Swap), or Tier 4 (Middle Added/Missing).
  8. Bank penny-drop name matches under Tier 1-4.
  9. Face-match score >= 0.75.
- **Autonomous Rework Request (Needs Info / Reupload):** Triggered when minor defects occur (e.g. blurry image, middle initial spelling variant, penny-drop name mismatch). All defects across all 5 documents must be bundled into a **single consolidated rework notification**.

head: 3.2 Decisions Reserved for Human Ops Reviewers (Human-in-the-Loop)
text:
1. **Hard Rejection on Identity (`NAME_MISMATCH`):** AI must **NEVER** issue an autonomous hard rejection for `NAME_MISMATCH`.
2. **Borderline Face Match (0.60 to 0.74):** Reviewed side-by-side by a human reviewer comparing lighting, angle, and age progression.
3. **Name Change After Marriage:** Requires human inspection of gazette notification or marriage certificate.
4. **Unrecognized Education Board:** Requires human verification against the Council of Boards of School Education (COBSE) directory.

head: Specimen Defect Taxonomy & Failure Modes Engineering Guide
text:
This guide details the failure modes, OCR degradation scenarios, biometric anomalies, and identity defects encountered in POSP onboarding documents, referencing the official 14 reason codes and 12 specimen cases.

---

head: 1. Defect Category Hierarchy
text:
```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Document Submission] --> B{Quality Triage}
    B -->|Blur / Glare / Crop / OCR < 0.75| C[REUPLOAD: Image Quality Defects]
    B -->|Quality OK| D{Statutory Eligibility Check}
    D -->|Underage / Non-individual PAN / Bad Format / Class 10 Fail / Registry Hit| E[REJECT: Hard Ineligibility]
    D -->|Eligible| F{Identity & Cross-Doc Consistency}
    F -->|Spelling Variant / DOB Mismatch / Bank Mismatch / Face < 0.60| H[NEEDS_INFO: Consolidated Rework]
    F -->|Tiers 1-4 Name + Clean Docs + Face >= 0.75| I[APPROVE: STP to Training]
```

---

head: 2.1 Image Quality Defects (Verdict: `REUPLOAD`)

| `IMAGE_BLURRY` | Laplacian variance < 100.0 or OCR word confidence < 0.75 | Camera shake, out-of-focus mobile capture, low lighting | Request new photograph in daylight | *"Your {doc_name} photo is blurry, and we could not clearly read required fields like {field_name}. Please retake in bright natural light with steady focus: {upload_link}"* |
| `IMAGE_CROPPED` | Edge detection fails to find 4 document corners; bounding box intersects canvas boundary | Applicant clipped card edge, cut off signature or DOB | Request full uncropped capture | *"A portion of your {doc_name} is cut off outside the camera frame. Please ensure all four corners and edges of the card are clearly visible: {upload_link}"* |

Please retake without camera flash or angle the phone away from direct lights: {upload_link}"* |

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `UNDERAGE` | `application_date - DOB < 18.0 years` | IRDAI Guidelines §4(a) | Terminal rejection. Account locked. | No. May reapply upon reaching age 18. |

| `NAME_SPELLING_VARIANT`| Jaro-Winkler >= 0.85 or Levenshtein <= 2 (e.g. `LAKSHMI` vs `LAXMI`) | Request supporting identity document or affidavit | Send consolidated WhatsApp/SMS notification; allow applicant to confirm canonical spelling |

head: 3. Ground Truth Calibration Rules
text:
1. **Rule of Single-Pass Rework:** If an application has both `IMAGE_BLURRY` on Marksheet and `BANK_NAME_MISMATCH` on Cheque, the system MUST emit a single notification itemizing both defects. Never ask for one document at a time.
2. **Rule of Human Confirmation for Rejection on Identity:** When `NAME_MISMATCH` is flagged, the system MUST NOT auto-reject without human review, ensuring false positives from OCR failures do not penalize genuine applicants.
3. **Informational Mismatches:** Address state discrepancies (`ADDRESS_STATE_MISMATCH`) between Aadhaar and declared form must NEVER trigger rework or rejection; they are informational only.

head: Consolidated Rework Engine & Bi-Lingual Communication Specification
text:
> **Engineering Specification for Single-Pass Rework Aggregation & Automated Messaging**  
> **Source:** Rulebook v3.2 §8 & Baseline Defect Pareto Analysis

---

head: 1. The Single-Pass Principle
text:
In historical operations, reviewers frequently issued fragmented rework queries (e.g., asking for a new marksheet on Monday, and then asking for a new bank cheque on Wednesday). This created severe applicant frustration, pushed average touches to 3.0, and drove a 33.2% dropout rate.

**The Single-Pass Rule:**
The system must inspect all 5 uploaded documents completely before dispatching any rework request. All defects across the entire application must be consolidated into a **single comprehensive message** containing targeted instructions and deep-links for each defective item.

---

head: 2.1 Image Quality Defects (`IMAGE_BLURRY`, `IMAGE_CROPPED`, `IMAGE_GLARE`)
text:
- **English:**
  > *"Dear {applicant_name}, your {document_name} photo could not be verified because {specific_defect_reason}. Please take a new clear photo in bright daylight ensuring all four corners are visible, and upload it here: {secure_reupload_link}"*
- **Hindi:**

head: 3. Targeted Deep-Link Architecture
text:
When an applicant opens the secure re-upload link:
1. The applicant is authenticated via a time-limited cryptographically signed session token (HMAC-SHA256, 72-hour validity).
2. The user interface displays **ONLY** the defective documents requiring correction.
3. Previously approved documents are rendered with a green `VERIFIED` lock icon and cannot be modified or re-uploaded, preventing re-triggering of completed reviews.

head: Name Matching Algorithm & Identity Taxonomy Specification
text:
> **Engineering Specification for the 8-Tier Identity Resolution Engine**  
> **Source:** Rulebook v3.2 §5 & Specimen Ground Truth Benchmark

---

head: 1. The 8-Tier Name Matching Taxonomy
text: Indian legal names exhibit diverse linguistic variations, patronymics, initializations, and honorific additions. Treating spelling variations as identity mismatches causes over 40% of unnecessary manual touches. PolicyNest implements an 8-tier resolution taxonomy:

head: 1. The 8-Tier Name Matching Taxonomy
text:
| Tier | Pattern Description | Golden Anchor (PAN) | Document Candidate | Verdict | STP Allowed? | Operational Action |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Tier 1** | **Exact Match** (case & space insensitive) | `RAHUL KUMAR SHARMA` | `Rahul Kumar Sharma` | **MATCH** | Yes | Auto-Approve |
| **Tier 2** | **Initials for Given or Middle Names** | `RAHUL KUMAR SHARMA` | `R K SHARMA` or `RAHUL K SHARMA` | **MATCH** | Yes | Auto-Approve |
| **Tier 3** | **Token Order Swapped** | `RAHUL KUMAR SHARMA` | `SHARMA RAHUL KUMAR` | **MATCH** | Yes | Auto-Approve |
| **Tier 4** | **Middle Name Added or Missing** | `RAHUL KUMAR SHARMA` | `RAHUL SHARMA` or `PRIYA KUMARI SHARMA` | **MATCH** | Yes | Auto-Approve |
| **Tier 5** | **Spelling Variant of Same Name** | `MOHAMMAD ASIF` | `MOHAMMED ASIF` or `LAKSHMI` vs `LAXMI` | **NEEDS_INFO** | No | Emit single-pass rework query (`NAME_SPELLING_VARIANT`) |
| **Tier 6** | **Surname Changed Post-Marriage** | `PRIYA SHARMA` | `PRIYA VERMA` | **NEEDS_INFO** | No | Request Marriage Certificate / Gazette (Human Review) |
| **Tier 8** | **Truncated Core-Banking Return** | `SACHIN CHAND MITTAL` | `S C MITTAL` | **MATCH** | Yes | Bank Penny-Drop auto-approval |

---

head: 2. Algorithmic Resolution Pipeline
text:
The Name Matching Engine executes a multi-stage deterministic comparison pipeline:

```text
[Input Strings: Name A (PAN), Name B (Doc/Bank)]
                     │
                     ▼
       Stage 1: Unicode Normalization
   (Strip honorifics: SHRI, SMT, MR, MS, DR;
    Uppercase; strip special characters; collapse whitespace)
                     │
                     ▼
         Stage 2: Exact Equality Check
           (A == B) ───[YES]───> Tier 1: MATCH
                     │ [NO]
                     ▼
         Stage 3: Token Sorted Equality
   (sorted(tokens_A) == sorted(tokens_B)) ───[YES]───> Tier 3: MATCH
                     │ [NO]
                     ▼
        Stage 4: Initial Expansion Match
   (Verify each initial in B corresponds to prefix of token in A) ───[YES]───> Tier 2: MATCH
                     │ [NO]
                     ▼
        Stage 5: Subsequence / Subset Match
   (tokens_B is strict subset of tokens_A or vice-versa) ───[YES]───> Tier 4: MATCH
                     │ [NO]
                     ▼
      Stage 6: Fuzzy & Phonetic Distance
   (Jaro-Winkler >= 0.88 OR Levenshtein distance <= 2 OR Double Metaphone match)
                     │
         ┌───────────┴───────────┐
      [YES]                     [NO]
        │                         │
        ▼                         ▼
Tier 5: SPELLING_VARIANT     Tier 7: DIFFERENT PERSON
```

---

head: 3. Strict Compliance Guardrail: Zero AI False Accusations
text:
Under PolicyNest Governance Rule §9, the Decision Engine is **strictly forbidden from issuing an autonomous terminal rejection under Tier 7 (`NAME_MISMATCH`)**.
- **Rationale:** OCR artifacts, inverted identity documents (e.g. uploading a parent's document by accident), or transliteration failures could unjustly disqualify a valid applicant.
